title: The patient letters and the audit
scenario:
You are the operations director of a dental chain with 40 clinics and 1,300 staff. A new tool drafts letters to patients from treatment notes. The letters contain health details.

The tool runs on Anthropic's API. Legal has three requirements. IT has filled in a status sheet. You must review it before launch.
exhibit:
Compliance review: patient letter tool (made-up example data)

Legal asks
  L1  Model processing stays in the US.
  L2  Patient health details only with a signed health-data agreement.
  L3  Show who changed settings, and when.

IT status
  S1  The developer team sets inference_geo to "us" in its own code.
      Marketing's key in the same workspace sends no geo setting.
      Workspace allowed geos: not set.
  S2  Expected token cost at the standard rate: $12,000 a month.
      Model: Claude 4.6 or later.
  S3  BAA signed. Organization is HIPAA-enabled.
      Next week a developer wants to add a new API feature.
      The feature is not marked eligible in the vendor's feature table.
  S4  Compliance API (Activity Feed) switched on today, 6 Oct.
      Auditor asks: "Who changed workspace settings on 29 Sept?"

questions.prompt: Line S1 does not meet requirement L1 for every key. Which fix works?

options.text: Set the workspace geo to US, because that decides where each request is processed.
options.explanation: Workspace geo controls where data is stored at rest, and it is set when the workspace is created. Inference geo controls where the model runs.

options.text: Limit the workspace's allowed inference geos to US and set its default geo to US.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic's page says these workspace settings enforce a geo policy across all keys in the workspace. A request for a geo outside the list returns an error.

options.text: Ask the marketing team to add the same geo setting to its own code as well.
options.explanation: That depends on each team remembering. A workspace restriction is enforced for every key, so nobody can forget.

options.text: Move the tool to an older model, because older models always run in the US.
options.explanation: Anthropic's page says older models do not support the inference geo setting at all. A request that includes it returns a 400 error.

questions.prompt: Finance asks for the monthly token cost with US-only processing. Anthropic's page (checked 2026-10-06) is the source. What is the number?

options.explanation: That is the standard rate. The page says US-only inference costs more on Claude 4.6 and later models.
That adds only $100, less than 1%. The page says the multiplier is 1.1x, which is 10% more.
Right. The page prices US-only inference at 1.1x the standard rate for Claude 4.6 and later models. $12,000 x 1.1 = $13,200.
That doubles the cost. The documented multiplier is 1.1x, not 2x.

questions.prompt: Line S3: what should the developer do before adding the new feature?

options.text: Check the eligibility table first, and leave the feature out until it is marked eligible.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic's page says a HIPAA-enabled organization gets an error for a non-eligible feature. OpenAI also lists limits for its BAA-eligible endpoints and features.

options.text: Add it, because a signed BAA covers every single feature of the vendor's API.
options.explanation: Anthropic's page says its feature table lists which features are eligible. The signed BAA is the source of truth, and not every feature is covered.

options.text: Add it, because the API will quietly ignore any feature that the BAA does not cover.
options.explanation: The page says the API returns a 400 error instead. It does not ignore the feature.

options.text: Try it on real patient letters at one clinic first, and ask legal after the trial ends.
options.explanation: This sends patient health data through a feature that may not be covered. Legal and the eligibility table come first.

questions.prompt: Line S4: the auditor asks about 29 Sept. What is accurate?

options.text: The Activity Feed fills in older activity once enabled, so 29 Sept will appear soon.
options.explanation: Anthropic's page says recording is not retroactive. Activity from before enablement is not backfilled.

options.text: The feed keeps 6 years of history, so a change on 29 Sept will be in it.
options.explanation: The 6 years apply from the day recording starts. Nothing before 6 Oct was recorded.

options.text: Tell the auditor no change was made, because the feed shows nothing for that day.
options.explanation: An empty feed before 6 Oct means nothing was recorded, not that nothing happened. That statement could be false.

options.text: The feed starts on 6 Oct, so it can't show 29 Sept; find other records and keep logging on.
options.explanation: Right. Recording starts when the Compliance API is first enabled. The lesson's rule is to turn audit logging on before launch.
